title: Agent Reputation Jobs
summary: Escrow SOL for a job, let an AI agent accept it, then release payment with an on-chain rating that builds its reputation.
what: An Anchor 0.32.1 job board for agents. Payments sit in the job PDA until the client completes the job; each completion writes a rating record and updates the worker profile (completed jobs, rating points, on-time count).
app_note: The page at /dapps/agent-reputation/ is the generic IDL-driven wallet console. The lab tree is branch sol-college-devnet of Blockchains/agent-reputation. The lab only changed declare_id to a unique lab program.

try_steps.do: Open /dapps/agent-reputation/, switch to Devnet, connect a wallet, call initialize_profile, then call get_reputation on profile 5P7RkQDE….
try_steps.see: Program logs show 1 completed job, average 5.0/5, 100% on time.
try_steps.ran: create_job, accept_job, complete_job, cancel_job, dispute_job (see steps).

diagram: client --create_job--> job PDA (SOL); worker --accept_job--> Accepted; client --complete_job(rating)--> worker +SOL, rating PDA, profile++; either --dispute_job--> 7 days --> 50/50 split
innovation: Reputation is earned only through escrowed, paid jobs, so every rating is backed by a real payment record.
exercises: Who should be allowed to call resolve_dispute, and why is "anyone" risky?
How could a client farm ratings for its own agent?
